Is gold's recovery above $4,000 enough to fix a broken market? asks Michele Schneider
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - After last week’s sharp selloff, the gold market has managed to reclaim the $4,000 level. While this is an important hurdle that needs to be cleared, one market strategist says the precious metal still has significant work to do to undo the recent technical damage. In an interview with Kitco News, Michele Schneider, Chief Market Strategist at MarketGauge, said that she is watching the $4,000 level carefully as it could provide an attractive entry point. However, she added that patience is required as she sees significant signs that the gold and silver markets have broken. Schneider, who has been a long-term gold bull, said that she currently holds no positions in either gold or silver. She explained that she took profits on her gold holdings in August and was subsequently stopped out of her remaining position. She has stayed on the sidelines ever since.

'This is that gift': why Lobo Tiggre is buying uranium as contract prices hit a record
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The Independent Speculator sold most of his gold and silver stocks early this year. Now he's spending cash on uranium, and says he'll "lean heavy into silver" when the time comes. NEW ORLEANS - Lobo Tiggre sold most of his gold and silver stocks early this year, when, he said, gold was about $1,500 an ounce higher than it is now. He has been sitting on a big pile of cash since. Now he's spending some of it. Just not on gold. "It turns out that the first opportunity since I sold this year, big opportunity, like clear, obvious buying opportunity, has been in uranium," Tiggre, founder of The Independent Speculator, told Kitco News on Oct. 29 at the New Orleans Investment Conference.

Gold is being treated ‘like an AI stock, which it's not,' says Peter Boockvar
items.summaryEn: The OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners CIO said gold ’s drop below $4,000 looked like forced selling. Days later, gold is back above $4,000 after the midterms, and he says investors shouldn’t count on the Fed to rescue the AI trade. NEW ORLEANS (Kitco News) - Gold fell more than $120 an ounce on Oct. 30 and broke below $4,000. To Peter Boockvar, it didn’t look like a broken thesis. It looked like a forced seller. “ Gold ’s not trading on its own fundamentals. There’s a forced seller out there, whether it’s margin-driven or whatever,” the chief investment officer at OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners told Kitco News at the New Orleans Investment Conference on Oct. 30.

Gold holding firm as US ISM says Service Sector expands in October
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to hold critical support above $4,000 an ounce, but steady activity in the U.S. services sector highlights the ongoing challenges for the precious metal, as a resilient economy and persistent inflation give the Federal Reserve room to maintain its tightening bias. The Institute for Supply Management (ISM) announced Wednesday morning that its Services Purchasing Managers Index came in at 54.5 in October, down slightly from 54.9 in September. The data was modestly weaker than expected, as economists were looking for a roughly unchanged reading of 54.8. Although momentum in the services sector continues to slow, activity remains in expansion territory. Readings above 50 in such diffusion indexes signify economic growth, while readings below 50 indicate contraction. The farther an indicator is above or below 50, the greater the rate of expansion or contraction.
